method: Fresh comparison of exact frozen-English and Gujarati blocks, with reverse paraphrases focused on construction level, quotient type, quantifier order, algebraic operation direction, bounds, proof dependencies and all four disclosed source repairs.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The chapter constructs standard number systems inside naïve set theory and credits the source work.
samples.assessment: Scope, foundational setting and attribution are all retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Integers arise from ordered pairs of naturals representing differences, but equal differences require quotienting.
samples.assessment: The two motivating observations and the need for equivalence classes remain distinct.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Literal ordered pairs are too fine because different pairs can represent the same integer.
samples.assessment: The 0−2 and 4−6 example has the same equality and inequality directions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Pairs are equivalent exactly when cross-addition gives a+d=c+b, and this relation must be reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
samples.assessment: The biconditional and all three equivalence-relation obligations are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Transitivity follows by combining two cross-sum equalities and cancelling their common natural-number terms.
samples.assessment: All variables, equations and the cancellation step are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An integer is an equivalence class of ordered pairs of naturals under the defined relation.
samples.assessment: The quotient object and set-builder formula have the correct level.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Addition, multiplication and order on integer classes are defined by representative formulas.
samples.assessment: Representatives, operation directions and nonnegativity condition retain exact math parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Natural numbers are embedded into the constructed integers using n↦[n,0].
samples.assessment: Embedding direction and the warning that the original naturals are not literally members of the quotient are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Rationals are equivalence classes of integer pairs with nonzero denominator under cross multiplication.
samples.assessment: The nonzero restriction, ordered-pair type and equivalence formula are all present.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Rational addition and multiplication use the usual fraction formulas; order uses s−r nonnegative.
samples.assessment: OLARI-001 repairs only the reversed subtraction in the source gloss and agrees with the displayed definition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Integers embed into rationals through i↦[i,1], and the operations and order behave compatibly.
samples.assessment: The embedding and its intended preservation properties are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The next construction must distinguish the real line from the rationals before building reals.
samples.assessment: The chapter transition and comparison target are faithful.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Both rationals and reals are ordered fields, but the reals contain square root of two while the rationals do not.
samples.assessment: The shared structure and decisive counterexample are not conflated.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Assuming sqrt(2)=m/n in lowest terms leads to a contradiction.
samples.assessment: Quantifiers, lowest-terms condition and reductio framing survive.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The geometric parity proof decomposes squares and shows both m and n must be even.
samples.assessment: The figure reference and parity dependence remain correctly directed.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The formal parity proof derives m=2r and then n even from m²=2n².
samples.assessment: Every algebraic substitution and divisibility conclusion is unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Rationals have gaps that the reals fill, motivating a structural completeness condition.
samples.assessment: The metaphor remains subordinate to the formal property.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The rationals below sqrt(2) are bounded but have no rational least upper bound.
samples.assessment: The set, bound and failure of leastness have the correct number system and order direction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The continuum should fill every such gap, expressed by the least-upper-bound completeness property.
samples.assessment: Nonempty and bounded hypotheses are retained without adding completeness to the rationals.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A real point splits rationals into a lower part and an upper part.
samples.assessment: Both halves and strict order directions are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A rational cut is identified by its lower portion, an initial segment without a greatest member.
samples.assessment: The lower-side convention and no-maximum condition are explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A cut is a nonempty proper initial segment of rationals with no greatest element.
samples.assessment: All four defining conditions and their symbolic expansion remain.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The cut representing sqrt(2) consists of negative rationals and rationals whose square is below two.
samples.assessment: Both disjuncts and the deferred verification remain.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Order on cuts is inclusion and real numbers are defined as cuts.
samples.assessment: The inclusion direction and identity of the real domain are correct.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The set of cuts satisfies the completeness property.
samples.assessment: The theorem states the intended quotient construction result without weakening it.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For a nonempty bounded set of cuts, its union is a cut and its least upper bound.
samples.assessment: OLARI-002 invokes nonemptiness for member existence; properness, initiality, no maximum and leastness all remain intact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Rationals embed as principal cuts and operations on cuts are defined by set operations with sign cases.
samples.assessment: The embedding, operation formulas and sign-sensitive branches retain formula parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Completeness separates reals from rationals, while the cut construction gives analysis a rigorous foundation.
samples.assessment: The mathematical and philosophical claims stay properly qualified.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Decimal and Cauchy constructions may be equally rigorous; the decisive gain is understanding completeness.
samples.assessment: The comparison does not claim one representation uniquely constitutes the reals.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: After constructing integers, rationals and reals, ordinary proofs deliberately forget their set-theoretic encodings.
samples.assessment: The hierarchy of constructions and pragmatic conclusion are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Competing encodings undermine the claim that one set-theoretic construction reveals what numbers metaphysically are.
samples.assessment: The Benacerraf-style underdetermination argument remains conditional rather than asserted as a theorem.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The constructed natural and integer zeros are unequal, so the construction does not literally make naturals a subset of rationals.
samples.assessment: The type distinction and counterintuitive consequence are explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Naïve set theory can host the theories of integers, rationals and reals once naturals are given.
samples.assessment: The relative-foundation claim is preserved without overstating philosophical significance.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A commutative ring has two constants and two operations satisfying eight displayed axioms.
samples.assessment: All eight formulas and their universal restriction to S have exact parity; translated axiom labels do not alter math.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Integer addition is associative because representative addition reduces to associativity on naturals.
samples.assessment: Representative choices and every equality in the calculation match.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Swapping a representative pair gives an additive inverse whose sum is the zero class.
samples.assessment: The equivalence relation witness and zero-class conclusion are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Distributivity of integer classes follows from the expanded representative multiplication formula.
samples.assessment: The long componentwise calculation has exact formula parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An ordered ring also carries a total order compatible with addition and multiplication by nonnegative elements.
samples.assessment: The footnote retains reflexivity, transitivity, antisymmetry and comparability, plus trichotomy.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The two displayed implications specify order compatibility in a ring.
samples.assessment: Both implication directions and the nonnegative multiplier premise are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An ordered field is an ordered ring in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.
samples.assessment: The universal nonzero restriction and existential inverse formula are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The sum of two cuts is a nonempty proper initial segment with no maximum.
samples.assessment: Each cut condition is established with the same witnesses and inequalities.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The proposed sqrt(2) cut has no maximum because q=(2p+2)/(p+2) lies above p while q² remains below two.
samples.assessment: Both inequality chains and the role of positive rational p are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The Cauchy construction is an alternative to Dedekind cuts and has a distinct nineteenth-century history.
samples.assessment: The named contributors and historical attribution are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Decimal expansions can be modeled as functions on naturals, with adjustments for the integer part and repeating nines.
samples.assessment: Function direction, digit indexing and the 0.999… example remain.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Increasingly accurate rational approximations motivate sequences; an alternating zero-one function fails to approach a real limit.
samples.assessment: All three numbered insights, parity cases and the motivating failure are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A rational-valued sequence is Cauchy when every positive rational epsilon eventually bounds all pairwise tail differences.
samples.assessment: Quantifier order, rational epsilon, natural cutoff and strict inequality are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Different Cauchy sequences can encode the same real when they differ only finitely at the start.
samples.assessment: The f/g example and intended sameness of limit remain qualified.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Two Cauchy sequences are equivalent when their difference tends to zero, and reals are the resulting equivalence classes.
samples.assessment: OLARI-003 repairs ‘relations’ to ‘classes’; the definition of tending to zero and the equivalence relation remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Constant rational sequences embed rationals, while pointwise addition and multiplication define operations on real classes.
samples.assessment: The embedding and both pointwise formulas preserve representatives and operation order.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A nonzero real class is positive when its representative is eventually positive; order is defined through g−f.
samples.assessment: OLARI-004 repairs rational zero to real zero and leaves the eventual-positivity quantifiers unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The quotient classes of Cauchy sequences, rather than raw sequences, are asserted to form an ordered field.
samples.assessment: The theorem/exercise category repair is covered by OLARI-003.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every nonempty upper-bounded set in the construction is asserted to have a least upper bound.
samples.assessment: Nonemptiness, boundedness and leastness all remain.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Bisection defines decreasing upper approximants f and increasing lower approximants g whose difference tends to zero.
samples.assessment: Both recursive cases, midpoint and equality of quotient classes are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The class of f is an upper bound, proved by contradiction using an eventual constant approximation.
samples.assessment: Order directions and the contradiction with construction are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Any class below g fails to be an upper bound because some member of S lies above a corresponding g(n).
samples.assessment: The increasing-sequence argument and final leastness conclusion are preserved.
